'''Émile Alphonse Louis Merlin''' (12 October 1875 in [[Mons, Belgium|Mons]] – 29 July 1938 in [[Le Bourg d'Oisans]]) was a Belgian mathematician and astronomer.

Merlin attended the secondary school ''Athénée royal de Bruxelles''. He then studied at the University of Liège and the [[Ghent University|University of Ghent]], where in 1900 he received his doctorate in mathematics. This was followed by a stay abroad between 1901 and 1903 in Paris at the Sorbonne, at the [[Collège de France]] and in Göttingen. In 1904, he became an assistant at the observatory in [[Uccle]]. In 1909, he was promoted to astronomer adjoint. From 1912, he was a lecturer on astronomy and geodesy at the University of Ghent and in 1919, he became a full professor and director of the geographical station of the University of Ghent.<ref name=Obit>{{cite journal|bibcode=1938C&T....54..295V|title=Nécrologie: Emile Merlin (1875-1938)|last1=Van Aerschodt|first1=L.|journal=Ciel et Terre|year=1938|volume=54|page=295}}</ref>

He was an alpinist and died in a mountain accident in the French Alps in Le Bourg d'Oisans.<ref name=Obit/>

Merlin was one of the editors for the French edition of [[Klein's encyclopedia]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Merlin, É|chapter=Configurations|title=Encylopédie des Sciences Mathématiques, ''Edition française''|year=1913|pages=144–160|volume=Tome 3, volume 2}}</ref>

For his work on celestial mechanics, he was awarded the A. de Potter Prize of the Royal Belgian Academy of Sciences. He was president of the Belgian Mathematical Society, an honorary member of the Astronomical Society of Mexico and a member of the Commission for Mathematics and Astronomy of the National Fund for Research in Spain.<ref name=Obit/> He was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Toronto 1924 (''Sur les lignes asymptotiques en géométrie infinitésimale'') and Oslo 1936 (''Sur certains mouvements des fluid parfaits'').

==Selected publications==
* with Paul Stroobant, Jules Delvosal, Hector Philippot, and Eugène Delporte: {{cite book|title=Les observatoires astronomiques et les astronomes|publisher=Hayez|year=1907|url=https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.376973}}
* {{cite journal|title=La Répartition des Taches Solaires en Latitudes Héliographiques|year=1907|bibcode=1907BSBA...12A.179M|last1=Merlin|first1=E.|journal=Bulletin de la Société Belge d'Astronomie|volume=12|pages=A179}}
* {{cite journal|title=Sur la détermination systématique des éléments de la figure elliptique d'une planète au moyen de mesures micrométriques de diamètres|year=1908|bibcode=1908AN....178..391M|doi=10.1002/asna.19081782404|last1 = Merlin|first1 = E.|journal = Astronomische Nachrichten|volume = 178|issue = 24|pages = 391–394|url = https://zenodo.org/record/1424855}}                                                                   	
* {{cite journal|title=Observations d'etoiles doubles effectuees a l'equatorial de 38 centime tres EN 1906 et 1907|year=1908|bibcode=1908AnOBN..11...75M|last1 = Merlin|first1 = Emile|journal = Annales de l'Observatoire Royal de Belgique Nouvelle Serie|volume = 11|page = 75}}
* {{cite journal|title=Sur la résolution graphique des triangles sphériques et la détermination rapide de la longitude et de la latitude d'un lieu|year=1930|bibcode=1930BuAst...6..119M|last1 = Merlin|first1 = Émile|journal = Bulletin Astronomique|volume = 6|page = 119}}	
* {{cite journal|title=Sur une formule usitée en astronomie|year=1938|bibcode=1938C&T....54....1M|last1 = Merlin|first1 = E.|journal = Ciel et Terre|volume = 54|page = 1}}
